paper_metadata.title: New β-type Ti-Zr-V-Nb alloys used for laser-based direct energy deposition: Design, microstructure, and properties

evidence.quote: To develop new titanium alloys for laser-based direct energy deposition, Ti-Zr-V-Nb alloys were designed from a basic Ti60.94Zr39.06 congruent composition alloyed with constant V content and varying Nb contents.
In this respect, the Ti60Zr40 congruent alloy is a good candidate since it has a single melting temperature, which gives it high structure stability and good formability.
Ti60.94Zr39.06 congruent composition alloyed with constant V content and varying Nb contents.

the final parameters were chosen: laser power 2.2 kW, scanning velocity 10 mm/s, laser diameter 4 mm, powder feed rate 5.4 g/min, and overlap rate 50%. After 17 layers of deposition, rectangular specimens with dimensions of 35 mm × 25 mm × 20 mm were built.

the strength of the studied alloys mainly arises from solid solution hardening, grain refinement, and dislocation strengthening.
Another significant strengthening mechanism is grain refinement strengthening. The grain refinement strengthening obeys the Hall-Petch relationship
Furthermore, dislocation strengthening arises when dislocations sliding on different slip planes intersect each other.
In the L-DED process, when the local melting pool begins to solidify, a constituent supercooling zone is formed in front of the solidus-liquidus interface due to the solute redistribution effect
The mechanism of abrasive wear is a micro-cutting action of the abrasive particles.
